habitat: Pairs and small parties in dense bushveld, forest fringes and thorn and grass tangles. Moister and shadier than Jameson’s Firefinch.
summary: A common resident. The bill looks black in the field. The colour line gives a red face, throat, breast, flanks and rump, and grey-brown upper parts including the crown. The male is identified by the grey crown and nape and a blackish belly. In Zimbabwe the crown and nape are washed pink, and the wings and mantle are browner than Jameson’s Firefinch. The female is not described. The call is a trilling bell-like phrase of chit-chit-chit ending wink-wink-wink, plus a stuttering alarm. The Kemp name is Bluebilled Firefinch and the code RB was left unchanged.

similar.note: Jameson’s Firefinch is the redder bird, with pink-washed upper parts. African Firefinch has a grey crown and, in the male, a blackish belly.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^16=65536 mature individuals (resident breeder); paper interval half–double → 32768–131072.

sources.title: Kemp A.C., Herholdt J.J., Whyte I. & Harrison J. (2001). Birds of the two largest national parks in South Africa: a method to generate estimates of population size for all species and assess their conservation ecology. S. Afr. J. Sci. 97: 393–403.

bill.shape: Blue-black. It looks black in the field.

head.pattern: Grey crown and nape. In Zimbabwe the crown and nape are washed pink.

upperparts.pattern: Grey-brown above. Wings and mantle browner than Jameson’s Firefinch.

underparts.pattern: Blackish belly. Red breast and flanks.

calls.description: A trilling, bell-like call of chit-chit-chit sounds ending wink-wink-wink, plus a stuttering alarm. Grade A call from the Pretoriuskop area of Kruger. The filename names African Firefinch.
